before: A regular expression describes a text pattern. Its test method returns true when the pattern matches.

Without boundaries, a pattern can match part of a longer string.
```javascript
console.log(/cat/.test("catalog"));
```
This is true.
^ marks the start of input. $ marks the end, with a special case that also allows a position before a final line terminator.
For this fixed-length code, also check text.length. That rejects an extra trailing line break even though $ can match just before it.
Use a pattern without g or y for this repeated validation task. Those flags make test depend on the expression’s lastIndex state.
Check the input is a string first, because test can otherwise convert nonstring values into text. This small rule is not an email or general identifier validator.
after: A regular expression describes a text pattern. Its `test` method returns `true` if the pattern matches and `false` if it does not.

A pattern can match just part of a longer string.
```javascript
console.log(/cat/.test("catalog"));
```
Output:
```text
true
```
The word catalog begins with cat, so the pattern finds a match.

`^` marks the start of the whole input. `$` marks its end.

With the `m` flag, these can also mark line boundaries. Our whole-code check uses no flags, so extra characters or a final line break do not fit.

`[0-9]` matches one digit from 0 through 9. `{3}` requires exactly three of them.
```javascript
const code = /^BOX-[0-9]{3}$/;
console.log(code.test("BOX-123"));
```
Output:
```text
true
```
The pattern requires BOX-, three digits, and nothing else.

Your project uses a shorter code: `ID-` followed by exactly two digits. Its length is five characters.

You may check that length explicitly too. The start and end markers, without the `m` flag, already require the pattern to cover the whole input.

Keep this validation pattern free of the `g` and `y` flags.

Those flags make repeated tests remember a position in `lastIndex`. Our check should give the same answer every time for the same text.

Complete `isRecordCode(text)`. First check that the input is a string, since `test` can otherwise convert values to text.

Accept only uppercase `ID-` and two digits from 0 to 9. Return a Boolean. Do not accept extra spaces, line breaks, or other digit characters.
